definition: Impel means to drive or urge someone forward to take action.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word impel. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know impel should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The smell of smoke impelled the night guard to leave his booth and check every floor.
A nudge is the gentlest push — a hint that you might act — and it stops well short of impel, which is real pressure that sets you moving.
Compel goes further than impel: what impels you presses you to act, but what compels you leaves no real choice at all.

Drive is the everyday word for pushing someone toward an act, and it covers almost any pressure — ambition, fear, a deadline. Impel is its formal cousin and names the felt push itself, in a fixed frame: something impels someone to do something.

To urge is to press someone with words and encouragement — a coach urges the team on. Impel needs no speaker at all: feelings or circumstances supply the push, and you can be impelled to act without anyone saying a word.

A prod is a small, repeated poke toward action — reminders, pointed questions — and it is far gentler than impel. What impels you is one strong push you feel; what prods you just keeps tapping until you finally move.
to hold an urge or action back rather than push it forward
to drain someone's will to act — the push running in reverse
